text:
lina: Heads up — release candidate 2026.03.20 is blocked. CI failing at the publish/verify step against our private npm registry; artifacts aren't being stamped/promoted. Error looks like 401 Unauthorized from the registry. Anyone on this?

ci-bot: Pipeline #789 - stage 'publish' failed: npm ERR! code E401
npm ERR! 401 Unauthorized - GET https://internal-registry.redwood.ai/-/npm/v1/security/audits/important

sam: I got a rotation alert from security-ops ~12:01 UTC — they rotated the service token for internal-registry-ci. Might be the token Jenkins still has cached.

security-ops: Confirmed. We rotated the CI service token at 12:01 UTC due to scheduled expiry and wrote the new secret to vault: secret/ci/npm-token. We did not have an automated sync to k8s secrets for the Jenkins namespace.

matt: Workaround: we can manually update the k8s secret 'ci-npm-token' in cluster-ci and restart the pipeline agent pod. That should let the publish step authenticate. But that is a manual change during a release window — want sign-off.

lina: Can someone confirm the risk/rollback plan if we manually patch the secret? Are there audit constraints?

jen: I can patch the secret and re-run the job. Need a security-ops thumbs-up to proceed so it's annotated in the audit.

security-ops: Approved for a one-time manual secret update with rotation-annotation. Use the vault ref and annotate the k8s secret with 'rotation=manual;ticket=#infra-492'. Also recommend re-running with the env override: ci-run --env TOKEN_FROM=vault:secret/ci/npm-token so it pulls directly.

sam: K8s secret updated and agent pod restarted. Re-triggering pipeline now.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy triggered for 2026.03.20-rc1 -> status: STARTED

ci-bot: Manual run #790 - publish step passed authentication, but promote step is stuck at 'verify-signature' with: 
```
verify-signature: expected etag=0xabc123 got etag=0xdef456
registry: 409 Conflict - ETag mismatch
```

matt: That looks like a propagation/cache inconsistency on the registry after the earlier failed publish attempts. Try invalidating the artifact cache and re-run promote.

jen: I'll purge the registry cache for that artifact path and bump the promote timeout. Doing: curl -X PURGE 'https://internal-registry.redwood.ai/registry/artifacts/<pkg>@rc' -H 'X-Auth: vaultref'

sam: Re-run promote after purge.

deploy-bot: Canary started health checks.

deploy-bot: Canary status update: 2/3 pods failed readiness within 120s -> Canary FAILED. Rolling back to previous stable.

lina: So even after auth fix and cache purge, the canary rolled back due to readiness failures. Is that related or a separate flaky?

matt: That readiness issue looks like an unrelated integration flake that surfaces when registry operations are slow. I see an intermittent registry timeout in the logs right before readiness probes fail. Suggest waiting ~10 minutes for the registry to settle and then re-run a controlled canary.

jen: I'm preparing a small infra PR to pin the npm client used in the pipeline (we saw a caching/auth bug with npm v9.x). PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/492 — pins to 8.19.3 and adds better retry/backoff for publish.

sam: After the secret update and the pinned-client PR merged to infra, I kicked off another manual pipeline: build -> publish -> promote. Publish succeeded; promote completed after retry. No etag mismatch this time.

deploy-bot: Manual pipeline #792 completed: publish and promote succeeded. Canary deploy triggered.

deploy-bot: Canary health checks passing. 5m stable. Rolling out to 50%.

lina: Good. Proceed to 100% when 15m observability looks clean.

sam: Rolled to 100%. Release unblocked. Summary for release notes: blocked by token rotation that wasn't propagated to k8s secrets, caused auth failures during publish; followed by registry cache propagation causing an etag mismatch on promote; mitigations — manual secret sync, registry cache purge, pinned npm client in CI, increased promote retries/timeouts.

jen: Follow-ups: infra PR merged; I also added a Jenkins job that pulls token from vault at job start and writes to ephemeral secret for the pod (automated).

matt: I'll open an alert runbook entry: alert on 'secret-expiry' and auto-sync hook for vault->k8s.

lina: Thanks all. Marketing/ops: please note the short release delay and that no customer data was exposed. Documenting incident in release notes and ops runbook.

security-ops: Audit: token rotated and manual update annotated in vault and k8s. Closing the incident. :white_check_mark:
